newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran plans to boost rail, road networks.
newsitem.headline: Iran plans to boost rail, road networks.

text.p: Iran plans to triple the length of its railway network by the year 2020 when it can transport 800 million tonnes of goods and 580 million passengers by road and rail annually, Iranian officials said.

"By the year 2020, the Islamic republic of Iran would be capable of transporting 800 million tonnes of goods and 580 million passengers," Roads and Transport Minister Akbar Torkan told an international transportation industry exhibition called the Silk Road which opened in Tehran on Tuesday.
"To attain that goal the railroad grid will have to be expanded to 23,000 km (14,000 miles) and the road network stretched to over 300,000 km (190,000 miles)," he said.
Torkan, whose remarks were reported by Iran's official news agency IRNA on Wednesday, did not give the current size of the railway and road networks.
But Managing director of Iran's Railway Company, Sadeq Afshar, said at the meeting Iran had 7,740 km (4,810 miles) of railway.
Torkan said Iran earned $600 million from transportation last year, including $300 million from shipping, $150 million from ports and $90 million from surface transport.

IRNA quoted Ali Saeedlou, head of the Exports Promotion Centre, as telling the conference that Iran's "strategic location on the Silk Road...the access to the open seas, can serve as bridge between the Persian Gulf region, Central Asia and the continents of Europe and Asia".
Alongside the conference, railway officials from the Economic Cooperation Organisation (ECO) opened a three-day meeting in Tehran on Tuesday, IRNA said.
ECO groups Turkey, Pakistan, Afghanistan, Azerbaijan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan.

Afshar said Iran had plans to purchase 300 locomotives and 10,000 cargo wagons in the next five years to meet its growing needs. It will take delivery of 1,500 cargo wagons from an Iranian manufacturing company in the next few months.
Iran and China have signed a $125 million agreement to jointly manufacture 100 locomotives over the next five years.

IRNA quoted ECO's secretary-general, Turkey's Onder Ozar, as saying the opening of Bandar Abbas-Bafq railway and Mashhad-Sarakhs-Tajan railway had helped accelerate trade between ECO states and both South Asian nations and Europe.

In May last year a railway between Iran and Turkmenistan was opened to unite Europe and Asia and revive the old Silk Road route between the two continents. Official figures show the 300-km (190-mile) link from Mashhad in Iran to the Turksib railway in Turkmenistan should carry eight million tonnes of freight and one million passengers a year.
